# Review

How the review rules apply, for the Builder and the Reviewer. The tier criteria, the
sensitive-path floors, the finding categories and their mapping, the tier challenge and the
round-2 rules are `AGENTS.md`'s Code Review Rules, and this file doesn't restate them.

## The tier

- The change sets the tier, never the ticket or the author. The PR body's
  `Risk: <tier> — <reason>` line is the only record of the effective tier.
- **Raising.** The self-verification subagent, a review bot's tier challenge or the Reviewer
  may raise it, and the Builder updates the line. Reviews run under the lower tier don't
  count toward the new one.
- **Rejecting below high.** A Builder that wants to reject a review bot's Important finding
  at low or medium first raises the PR to high.
- **Lowering.** Only habit lowers a tier, in a PR comment. The Builder records it by
  updating the line, its reason linking habit's comment. Not even habit goes below the
  highest floor among the sensitive paths the PR touches; the governance gate enforces that.
- **Pure Upgrade.** An Upgrade is pure when exact comparison reports no differences and
  the record's confirmed part is unchanged from the default branch.
- A pure revert the governance gate confirms takes the low path (`builder.md`, Pure reverts).

## Minimum reviews

| | low | medium | high |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Self-verification | yes | yes | yes |
| Review bot | — | one: `bot-1` | one: `bot-1` |
| Reviewer session | — | when substituting for the bot or required alongside it, same vendor allowed (Review bots) | yes, a vendor different from every Builder session that pushed to the PR, judged by the session marks |
| Security review | — | — | when the change involves authentication, privacy or secret handling |
| Merge summary by | Builder | Builder; the Reviewer when one ran | Reviewer, or the Builder when it is waived, as the high-risk report |

- Minimums are floors: every review that runs on a head binds. A Reviewer substitutes for
  the bot only at medium, as Review bots below gives it.
- habit's waiver is the only way a required review goes unmet; a waived Reviewer session
  leaves the Merge summary to the Builder (Waivers).
- **Before any merge:** required checks green (the governance gate from the first PR after
  Initialize; an Initialize PR's evidence states it as not yet applicable); the evidence
  comment on the head; the `Risk:` line present; a Merge summary naming the head; no open
  Important finding from any review on the head; rerun-only passes checked as below.
- **High adds:** before-and-after evidence in plain words; each one-way door rehearsed on a
  copy, the result attached and its recovery performed once; every finding answered, Nits
  included; only the high part in the PR; habit's go-ahead after merge for each
  one-way-door step (`builder.md`, After merge).

## Session marks

A session mark is the session's own statement, for sessions and habit to read. It guards
against honest mistakes, not deliberate misstatements; Merge watch and the governance gate
do not check it. Each Builder marks at every tier, and each Reviewer at medium and high:

```text
Session: <role> — <harness>, <model>, <vendor> (<source>)
```

The role is Builder or Reviewer. The harness is where the session runs; the model is its
name in the session's own system prompt; the vendor is the model's maker, not a service
routing to it. The source is `from the harness` when that prompt supplies the model and
its vendor follows from the name. Record only the detail supplied: a family such as GPT-6
stays a family, never a guessed finer model name. Read the prompt, never a harness
configuration file: that file's default can differ from the session's choice.

When the prompt names no model, or its vendor is unclear, the session asks habit in a
mid-session request and records the answer with `(as habit said)`. The same source applies
when habit supplies a missing earlier Builder's mark.

## Rerun-only passes

Required checks here are the fixed governance gate plus the checks named in the governance
record. The gate is required from the first PR after Initialize. An Initialize PR, whose base
has no gate workflow, is judged by the record's confirmed checks that report on it; its
evidence and verification prose state the gate as not yet applicable. A required check that
failed, timed out or was cancelled on a head, then passed on that same head, is a
**rerun-only pass** unless a change to an input or configuration used by that check repairs
the failure. A rerun-only pass counts as unrepaired. An unrelated PR
edit is not a repair. A governance gate run after a PR body edit qualifies as repaired only
when the edit corrects the failed gate input, such as its Risk declaration.

The Reviewer and the Merge summary's writer inspect the required checks' run history on the
head, earlier attempts included: GitHub's default listing shows only the latest attempt.
Compare changes between attempts with the evidence comment, verifying that each claimed
repair addresses that check's failure. For each rerun-only pass, confirm the linked issue
is open and covers its cause; no linked open issue is an Important finding. The Builder
owns ticketing the cause (`builder.md`, step 9).

## Subagents with no conversation context

Self-verification and the security review each run in a subagent that receives none of the
starting session's conversation. Its task text carries everything it needs: its role, the
PR or diff, the ticket, the files to read and what to return. Ask for that explicitly when
starting it, in whatever terms the harness's subagent tool uses for passing no history.

## Review bots

The record's confirmed `review_bots` lists the enabled review bots, in preference order. A PR
is judged by the list on the default branch before it merges: the Builder, the Reviewer and
Merge watch read it there, never from the PR's head, so a PR that changes the list leaves its
own requirements as they were. With no record on the default branch at all, as at an
Initialize, the list the PR adds is the one, since there is no earlier list to lower. A
supported bot missing from the list is disabled: never requested, retried, awaited or
counted, and never reported as unavailable.

- **Filling the slot.** At medium and high the Builder asks for the first enabled bot. When
  it is unavailable, the next enabled bot takes the slot, a **fallback**. One bot completes
  the list's purpose: it is an order to try for one slot, not a count of required bots.
- **Requests.** A bot starts only on habit's request. The Builder hands habit each request,
  as its subsection below gives it, and again after each repair push.
- **Unavailable**: no completed review on the head within the bot's wait after one more
  request; an error or no quota is the same. A completed review with findings is completed.
- **No bot left at medium.** After reading the bot policy, check whether every enabled bot is
  unavailable or the list started empty. A Reviewer session substitutes only when one of
  these conditions holds. It may use the Builder's vendor. habit starts it from the
  Builder's Reviewer handoff. It posts the Comment review and a successful `Reviewer` status
  on the head, then writes a readable Merge summary with `reviewer=clear` and the slot as
  `no-provider(none)` or `unavailable(<last enabled bot>)`, the last enabled bot in the
  base record's ordered list. To use habit's slot waiver for this head, declare
  `waived(<bot>)` or `waived(none)` (Waivers and Merge summary). No session skips
  the review on its own authority.
- **No bot left at high.** Escalate to habit, who waits or waives the slot (Waivers).
  The Reviewer's review proceeds either way.
- **Triggers.** Only a request comment writes a bot's trigger, since any comment holding one
  starts the bot. Every other text, from PR bodies and evidence to answers, summaries and
  issues, names the bot without writing its trigger.

Everything specific to one provider sits in its subsection.

### The Codex review bot

- **Name** in the record and the Merge summary: `codex`.
- **Request**: `ghm pr comment <n> --body "@codex review"`, which habit runs. A PR comment to
  it only ever requests a review, never a task.
- **Wait**: 30 minutes.
- **Completed on the head**: its comment's `codex-review-state:v1` marker, whose
  `code_review.commit_sha` is the head and whose `code_review.status` is `completed`.
- **Findings** are its inline comments: P0 and P1 are Important, the rest Nits.
- **Codex security review** is an optional extra, offered in the Builder's Reviewer
  handoff only on a PR that is high for authentication, privacy or secret handling.
  habit may leave the request with no waiver. When it runs, its Medium and above findings
  are Important, the rest Nits. It is never a kind in the fixed `Required reviews:` line.
  It posts only findings at or above its threshold, so no posted finding is not a completed
  clean review.
  The Reviewer's security review stays required (Security review).

### Copilot code review

- **Name** in the record and the Merge summary: `copilot`.
- **Request**: habit, in the browser, adds Copilot as the PR's reviewer at the Lite effort,
  and again after each push. A request from the agent account is silently dropped, so no
  agent makes one.
- **Wait**: 15 minutes.
- **Completed on the head**: apply [Merge watch's Copilot evidence rules](../../.github/governance/merge_watch.py)
  to both records. Copilot's submitted review must have `is_copilot_code_review` true,
  `commit_id` equal to the head, and state `COMMENTED`, `APPROVED` or `CHANGES_REQUESTED`.
  Require a completed `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` check run whose `conclusion` is `success`.
  Verify the check came from Copilot's dynamic Actions workflow by matching the head, linked job
  and check suite.
- **Findings** carry no severity. One Copilot labels by the Code Review Rules' categories
  takes that category; an unlabelled one is Important until answered.
- **Conditions**, which nothing enforces: the repository setting that lets Copilot reviews
  count toward required approvals stays off, and Copilot's monthly AI credits are shared
  with habit's other use.
- **Never the only judge** of fixed content or an instruction file: such a change is at
  least medium. At medium, when Copilot's is the head's only completed bot review, an
  additional Reviewer is required and may use the Builder's vendor. That review cannot
  be waived. At high the required Reviewer judges it, and its waiver keeps this condition
  (Waivers). A PR touching a sensitive path
  whose only completed bot review is Copilot's says so in its Merge summary.
  On a v5 medium merge, Merge watch checks the merged change and completed reviews
  to establish whether that companion was required. It checks the summary for
  `reviewer=clear` and the historical agent account's successful `Reviewer` status on the
  head by merge time. A missing declaration is a summary miss. A missing status is a
  Reviewer miss. Unresolved evidence leaves the assessment incomplete.

## Review state

One state per review per head: clear, flagged (an Important finding is open), waived or
unavailable. A bot slot may also be filled by a fallback, or have no enabled provider. A
result for an older head never counts for this one, and only a completed review is ever
written as clear.

## Waivers

habit may waive one named required review, `self-verification`, `bot-1`,
`reviewer` or `security`, or one named required verification, a row of the repository's
verification table, for one PR at one head.

- **The approval** is habit's own PR comment, from the repository owner's account, whose
  first line is:

  ```text
  Waiver: <item> at <full head sha> — <reason>
  ```

  `<item>` is a review's kind, or `verification "<the row's text>"`; the SHA is all 40 hex
  digits. A session may draft the line for habit. A comment by any other account, the agent
  account's quoting habit included, and free text in a summary approve nothing.
- **A new head voids it.** The same waiver on the new head needs a new comment.
- **Never waived**: the required status checks, the `Risk:` line, the evidence comment and
  the Merge summary; nor a Reviewer session that a review bot's subsection keeps.
- **A waived Reviewer session** leaves the Merge summary to the Builder: it runs the checks,
  writes the summary, at high as the high-risk report, and gives the merge handoff.
- **No different vendor available.** A same-vendor review at high does not meet the
  Reviewer requirement. Only habit's existing `reviewer` waiver for that head, subject to
  all the limits here, lets the PR proceed without a qualifying Reviewer. A same-vendor
  review that runs still binds like any review on the head; the fixed line reads
  `reviewer=waived`, the Builder writes the high-risk report, and its evidence sentence
  says that the review ran on a Builder's vendor. If no review ran, say so.
- No agent writes, edits or widens a waiver, and a waiver authorizes no merge by an agent.
- Merge watch checks each review waiver's author, head and item after the merge. The Merge
  summary's writer checks a verification waiver the same way, and any condition a review
  bot's subsection puts on a Reviewer waiver.

## Exceptions

A change that adds or edits an exception to a review requirement or an authorization rule,
such as a waiver or a fallback, is checked at every place that states it: the decision
point, each machine-read grammar, the examples and the reports. A statement broader than the
narrowest one is an Important finding.

## Answering findings

- **Important.** Fix it and reply "Fixed in `<sha>`", or reject it with evidence: "Not
  fixing:" plus a command and its output, or a concrete fact. Then resolve the thread. A
  rejection of a bot's Important finding first raises the PR to high (The tier); the
  Reviewer judges each rejection and reopens one it disagrees with.
- **Nit.** Optional at low and medium; at high, answer each.
- **Pre-existing.** Never blocks. The Important-severity ones go into one `needs-triage`
  issue per PR, linked from the Merge summary.

## Rounds

- A round is every required review on one head plus the Builder's response.
  Self-verification is never a round: it runs before the PR opens and again on each new
  head.
- From round 2 a review narrows as the Code Review Rules' round-2 rules say.
- Any new head, a sync included, gets its bot slot's review again, through habit's requests,
  and, at high or when a Reviewer ran at medium, a Reviewer pass over the change. First the
  Builder reruns self-verification (`builder.md`, step 6) on that head, deals with its
  findings, then updates the evidence comment.
- After three rounds with an Important finding still open, the Builder escalates with the
  options: change approach, split, more rounds, or drop.

## Evidence comment

One PR comment by the Builder, bound to the head it names and updated on every new head:

- the head's full SHA;
- the session mark of every Builder session that pushed a commit to the PR, at every tier,
  kept on every head's update (Session marks);
- each verification command and its result;
- for a pure Upgrade, both facts in The tier's definition;
- for a required check that passed after a repair on this head, the failed run, the
  repair and why it fixes that check's failure;
- each required check's rerun-only pass on this head, with the failed run and the cause's open
  issue, or an explicit statement that there were none;
- the self-verification subagent's finding count, and how each finding was handled;
- each bot slot's state on this head, in the Merge summary's words, and each waiver's link;
- whether habit requested the optional Codex security review and what it posted;
- `pr`'s before-and-after evidence.

## Security review

At high, when the change involves authentication, privacy or secret handling, the
Reviewer runs a security-review subagent with no conversation context. Its task names the
diff against the merge-base, the ticket, and these checks: authentication and authorization
paths; credentials and Actions secrets, in code, logs, errors and CI output; trust in input
from users, PRs and the network; exposure of private data. It rates each finding:

- **HIGH**: exploitable as merged, or exposes a credential or private data;
- **MEDIUM**: a weakness that one further mistake or an unlikely condition would expose;
- **LOW**: hardening, with no exposure today.

The Code Review Rules map these ratings onto finding categories.

## Merge summary

Written by the Builder at low and medium, after the last clear review; when a Reviewer ran
at medium, that Reviewer writes it. At high the Reviewer writes the high-risk report, or
the Builder does when habit waived the Reviewer session (Waivers).

### Checks first

On the head the summary names, perform the history and issue checks in Rerun-only passes
and link each cause's open issue in the summary. Then check:

1. Check that each required review and every additional review the summary lists is clear
   on this head, substituted at medium (Review bots), or waived by habit for this head
   (Waivers). For a bot declared complete, verify the named provider's completion and
   position in the enabled list. For a clear Reviewer, verify the agent account's successful
   `Reviewer` status. A waiver supports only a waived declaration. Before using it,
   confirm that the review was required and eligible for a waiver on this PR and that
   habit's exact-head comment names the item.
2. At high, match each finding on the reviewed head, including Nits, to the Builder's
   answer on GitHub. Read the answer itself. A successful `Reviewer` status, a resolved
   thread or a mention in the report cannot supply it. On the same head, a reasoned answer
   to keep the current behavior can settle a Nit without a repair push.
   If any answer is missing, hold both the high-risk report and the pinned merge command.
   Wait as the harness permits, then reread the PR and check the answers again
   ([harness limits](../../AGENTS.md#how-to-start)). If the head changed, follow Rounds.
   Once all answers are present and the other merge requirements pass, publish the report
   and link each disposition to the Builder's answer.
3. For public and private repositories, run `python3 .github/governance/branch_rules.py`
   from the repository root as the agent account. Cite the current default branch, the
   active Gate and Merge IDs and the effective rule types belonging to each. Gate must
   supply deletion, non-fast-forward, pull request and required status checks, including
   `governance-gate` from GitHub Actions (integration ID 15368). Merge must supply the
   update restriction. Product checks retain their configured publishers.
4. Report each missing, mismatched or unreadable fact to habit in Chinese. For a disabled
   ruleset, have habit re-enable it. If its name is taken by a tag or push ruleset, have
   habit rename that ruleset. If its reported scope excludes the default branch, have
   habit correct the scope or rename the ruleset before rerunning the owner script. For an
   absent ruleset, missing rule or wrong gate publisher, have habit rerun the owner
   script. For an unreadable response, check agent access and retry. When GitHub
   specifically refuses private rules for lack of Pro, renew student verification or make
   the repository public. On Initialize, state that the owner script follows merge and the
   gate check applies from the next PR. Hand over the pinned merge command when the
   remaining merge requirements pass.

### On the PR

Post one English comment on the final head. Post a new comment when the head changes.
Use the first two header lines at low and medium. At high, write all three on consecutive lines.

```text
## Merge summary: <tier> at <full head sha>
Required reviews: <kind>=<state>, <kind>=<state>
Security review applies: <yes|no>
```

- Write `low`, `medium` or `high` and all 40 lowercase hex digits of the PR head.
  Write an Upgrade's summary under the policy on its base. A v4-to-v5 Upgrade uses the
  published v4 title with seven digits. The first PR governed by v5 uses the full head.
- At high, judge whether the change involves authentication, privacy or secret handling.
  On the third line write `Security review applies: yes` if it does and
  `Security review applies: no` otherwise. With `yes`, include `security=clear` or
  `security=waived` on the second line. A waiver requires habit's exact-head comment for
  `security`. With `no`, list `security=clear` only if a security review ran, otherwise
  omit the row. Record the optional Codex security review separately in the evidence comment.
- Kinds, in this order, each one the tier requires (Minimum reviews) and any other that ran:
  `self-verification`, `bot-1`, `reviewer`, `security`.
- `self-verification`, `reviewer` and `security` take `clear` or `waived`.
- For a completed slot, write `clear(<bot>)` for the first enabled bot or, at medium and
  high, `fallback(<bot>)` for a later one. When habit waives a required slot for this head, write
  `waived(<bot>)` for an enabled provider or `waived(none)` when none was left.
  At low, omit an unused optional slot. Reserve
  `unavailable(<bot>)` and `no-provider(none)` for the medium substitution below.
- A line that leaves out a kind the tier requires, or a bot slot's provider, doesn't read.
- At medium a substituting Reviewer appears as `reviewer=clear`; `bot-1` must be
  `no-provider(none)` or `unavailable(<last enabled bot>)`, the last enabled bot in the
  base record's ordered list. An earlier unavailable provider does not qualify.
  When the bot policy is known, `no-provider(none)` declares that the list was initially empty
  or all enabled bots became unavailable. Sessions still verify the actual requests and
  unavailability evidence.
- For example, on a high change involving privacy:

  ```text
  ## Merge summary: high at 1a954628a960aaef81d7b2d4521929579f3541e6
  Required reviews: self-verification=clear, bot-1=clear(codex), reviewer=clear, security=clear
  Security review applies: yes
  ```

  and at medium on a repository-owned change outside the instruction files, after
  the first enabled bot was unavailable:

  ```text
  ## Merge summary: medium at 1a954628a960aaef81d7b2d4521929579f3541e6
  Required reviews: self-verification=clear, bot-1=fallback(copilot)
  ```

  and at medium, after all enabled bots became unavailable (an initially empty list also
  qualifies), with a substituting Reviewer:

  ```text
  ## Merge summary: medium at 1a954628a960aaef81d7b2d4521929579f3541e6
  Required reviews: self-verification=clear, bot-1=no-provider(none), reviewer=clear
  ```

The rest of the comment is the terminal copy's first line and seven items, in English, with
the high-risk report's additions at high.

### In the terminal

In Chinese (`AGENTS.md`, Talking to habit and to other agents):

- **First line**: the tier, the verdict, and the Important, Nit and Pre-existing counts.
- **Seven items:**
  1. the tier and why;
  2. what changed, in three to five bullets;
  3. each acceptance criterion, met or not;
  4. the evidence, in plain words;
  5. each finding in one sentence, with its answer;
  6. what the checks don't cover;
  7. how to revert.
- **Item 4 also lists** each waiver, with its item, reason and link, and each fallback, in
  plain words.
- **The high-risk report adds** why the change is high, the rehearsal result, and each step
  awaiting habit's go-ahead, with what it does and whether it can be undone.
  Its evidence item adds one plain sentence naming each Builder's and the Reviewer's vendor,
  in both the terminal copy and the English copy; when the Reviewer is waived, follow Waivers.
- **At low and at medium when the Builder writes it**, use checkable facts for items 4
  and 5 and state whether a session independent of the Builder reviewed the change.
  At medium it also names the bot whose review ran, or states its exact-head waiver.

Neither copy points at code: no paths, line numbers, diffs or snippets.

### The merge handoff

In the terminal, after the summary, as its writer's final handoff (`handoff.md`), whose
conclusion the summary's first line gives:

1. **The pinned merge command**, for habit to run:
   `ghm pr merge <n> --admin --squash --match-head-commit <sha>`, with the full head SHA.
   It is the only governed merge path.
2. **At high**, use the original Builder's wait state (`builder.md`, After merge).
   A waiting Builder needs no reply. If it stopped under the wait fallback, habit may say
   “继续” in that chat for the same checks. If its state is unknown, give both instructions
   conditionally.
3. **Misses**, only when any is open: the count of open miss records,
   `gh issue list --label miss --state open`, and a start request for a Planner session in
   which habit invokes `retro` on the oldest.
4. **This session**: the Reviewer's can be closed; a Builder says whether it stays
   open, what it waits for and the words habit says on return.

What is dispatched next comes from the Planner's dispatch plan, never from this handoff.
Each start request takes the form `AGENTS.md`'s How to start gives.
